question.text: Per Section 14.14 (p. 423) of the workbook, ANY change in valuation methodology or approach by an AIF Investment Manager - including a switch of primary IPEV method - shall be treated as:

answer.text: Material only if NAV impact exceeds 5%
Requiring prior SEBI approval before implementation
A minor operational change; no disclosure required since IPEV permits multiple methods
A material change requiring compliance with SEBI disclosure and reporting guidelines and a PPM update

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 14.14 (p. 423) of the workbook, "any change in the valuation methodology or approach shall be construed as a material change significantly influencing the decision of the investor" and the AIF must comply with SEBI disclosure / reporting guidelines and update the PPM with details of the change. The stem is now anchored to that page-423 rule, so option D is uniquely correct. The Trap: Option A invents a 5% threshold not in the workbook. Option B confuses material-change disclosure with prior-approval items (SEBI approval is not required, only disclosure). Option C is the "IPEV permits any method" trap - IPEV flexibility does not override SEBI's disclosure rule on methodology changes. Note: The original stem described a specific IPEV-to-IPEV switch, which conflicts with p. 421's statement that changes within prescribed valuation guidelines / norms "should not be construed as a material change" (with old/new methodology disclosure to investors). The stem has been generalised to the page-423 rule on ANY change in methodology / approach, so the keyed answer is uniquely supported. Source: FINAL_Series-XIX-C_AIF Managers_Ver-Dec-2025.pdf, pp. 421-423.
